indices.titulo: Bitcoin, copper, stocks, yields all fall; gold rises

texto: Bitcoin is up 0.3% since 00:00 UTC and up 7.9% over 30 days.
In the past month its typical daily move was about 0.7%, so today is a quiet day so far.

What this is: one day's price change on CoinGecko's market feed. What this is not: a forecast. A month of gains or losses says little about the next month, and bitcoin has often swung 10% or more within a few weeks.
On 15 Oct the 10-year Treasury yield was 0.33 percentage points above the 2-year, so the curve is positive, the usual shape. In the last 90 days it stayed between 0.20 and 0.53 points.

What it has meant before: an inverted curve came before most US recessions since the late 1960s, usually by about 6 to 24 months, and it has also given false alarms. In past cycles the curve often turned positive again shortly before a recession began, so a positive curve on its own is no all-clear.

What it means for people: the 2-year (4.77%) follows what markets expect from the Fed over the next two years, and US mortgage and other long loan rates tend to follow the 10-year (5.10%). Together they set the tone for borrowing costs over the coming months.
